# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 28 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 1QHa (Cave 1), Col. 28 | **Condition:** very fragmentary (final column)

---

**28:1** [...] I thank You, O Lord, for You have [...] with Your servant [...]

**28:2** [...] and You have sustained me by Your mercies, and the-abundance-of [...]

**28:3** [...] Your compassion upon all who seek You in truth [...]

**28:4** [...] and You have not abandoned the-orphan, nor despised the-poor [...]

**28:5** [...] for Your strength is without limit, and Your glory has no measure [...]

**28:6** [...] and wonderful heroes are Your ministers, and [...] the-humble [...]

**28:7** [...] among those-who-are-cleansed in the-dust-of [...] Your servants [...]

**28:8** [...] You have raised-up from the-dust to the-eternal council [...]

**28:9** [...] and from a perverted spirit You have purified him to take-his-stand [...]

**28:10** [...] in the-station-of the-host-of the-holy-ones and to enter into community [...]

**28:11** [...] with the-congregation-of the-sons-of heaven, and You have cast for him an eternal lot [...]

**28:12** [...] and there is no mediator to restore [...] and to turn [...]

**28:13** [...] from Your wrath, and there is no returning for-those-who [...] against You [...]

**28:14** [...] forever and ever. Amen. Amen. [...]

**28:15** [...] Selah. [...]

---

*EMET notes: Column 28 is the final surviving column of 1QHa, very fragmentary. The text returns to the thanksgiving formula ("I thank You, O Lord") and recapitulates the scroll's core themes: divine mercy to the lowly, exaltation from dust to angelic fellowship, purification of the perverted spirit. The column closes with the double "Amen" and "Selah" — a liturgical conclusion. Construct chains preserved throughout.*
